newsitem.title: CANADA: Frost warning issued for Manitoba grainbelt.
newsitem.headline: Frost warning issued for Manitoba grainbelt.

text.p: A frost warning was issued for the entire Manitoba grainbelt for Monday morning and frost was also likely to strike northeastern North Dakota, Environment Canada said.

"Manitoba's the only frost warning out for the Prairies; Dauphin saw -3.0 Celsius for a couple of hours this morning and it could go to -3.0 randomly across Manitoba Monday morning," meteorologist Steve Smith told Reuters.
Manitoba harvested 31 percent of its wheat, barley, canola, flax and oats by September 9, the Canadian Wheat Board said.
Dry weather likely advanced the harvest through the weekend.
The average fall frost date for most of the Prairies is September 12 based on a 59-year study by Environment Canada, the University of Manitoba and Manitoba Agriculture.
"The frost would probably happen in the last few hours before dawn. It could occur in northeastern North Dakota but I doubt they'll get any frost in Minnesota," Smith said.
Minneapolis television Saturday reported a light touch of frost on northern corn fields Saturday morning.
North Dakota's spring wheat harvest was 79 percent complete by September 9, that state's agriculture statistics service said.
North Dakota produces most of the United States' spring wheat crop.
